reason: The supplied desktop hero and mobile full-page captures present a coherent Precision Instrument identity: strong headline, readable supporting proposition, two differentiated audience actions, hairline organization and a purposeful process figure. findings.evidence: submit() reports a thrown fetch as “Your message could not be sent” and immediately directs email fallback. src/lib/email.ts:76,92-100 also collapses provider timeout/network uncertainty into false; src/app/api/contact/route.ts:39-52 converts that to definitive failure and supplies no idempotency key. A provider may accept a message before its acknowledgement is lost. Conversely, contact-form.tsx:24-32 resets the form and claims success for any HTTP-success response, even null/malformed JSON. tests/e2e/public-journeys.spec.ts:46-52 covers only intercepted {ok:true}; the supplied passing log does not cover these contact outcomes.
findings.userImpact: An organization cannot tell whether MECG received its inquiry. Following the fallback or retrying can duplicate an already accepted message; a malformed successful response can erase the draft without a validated receipt.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate the expected success receipt before clearing inputs. Preserve the draft and say “We could not confirm whether your message was sent” for uncertain outcomes. Distinguish definite rejection from unknown delivery; use a stable inquiry/idempotency identifier for safe retries. Add focused checks for accepted-but-lost acknowledgements and malformed successful responses.
